title: What Vikings Ate and Drank
hook: Rotten shark and sour dairy kept them alive.

scenes.text: Surviving a harsh Scandinavian winter required eating preserved foods that smelled intense.
scenes.imagePrompt: Snow-dusted timber storehouse on a hillside above a frozen lake. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos

scenes.text: Fish was wind-dried until it was rock hard, then pounded with wooden mallets before eating.
scenes.imagePrompt: Wooden racks of hanging dried cod against a crisp northern sky. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos

scenes.text: They fermented shark and seal meat in gravel pits to prevent scurvy and vitamin deficiencies.
scenes.imagePrompt: Earthen storage cellar with large ceramic crocks and stone weights. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos

scenes.text: Dairy was preserved as skyr, a thick sour fermented milk product packed with protein.
scenes.imagePrompt: Wooden bowl filled with thick white skyr curd beside a horn spoon. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos

scenes.text: Every meal was washed down with ale or mead, because fermented drinks were safer than bad water.
